69409.sol: The solar spectrum has maximum intensity at an energy of about 1.5 eV. 71315.subject: Biology
71315.text: Geometric growth can be expressed mathematically by the equation W₁=W₀e^ rt . ' W₁ ' stands for ________.
71315.sol: The mathematical expression for geometric (exponential) growth is given by W₁ = W₀ e^ rt . In this equation: W₁ represents the final size (weight, height, number, etc.) after time t . W₀ represents the initial size at the beginning of the period. r represents the growth rate (relative growth rate). t represents the time of growth. e represents the base of natural logarithms. 80475.subject: Botany
80475.text: If the diploid chromosome number of typical angiosperm is 36 , what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm ?
80475.sol: The diploid chromosome number of the angiosperm is given as 2n = 36 . The haploid chromosome number is n = 36 2 = 18 . In typical angiosperms, the endosperm is formed by the process of triple fusion, where one haploid male gamete fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (formed by two haploid polar nuclei). Therefore, the ploidy level of the endosperm is triploid ( 3n ). The chromosome number in the endosperm will be 3n = 3 18 = 54 .

84115.subject: Zoology
84115.text: Given below are four statements (A-D) regarding human blood circulatory system A. Arteries are thick-walled and have narrow lumen as compared to veins. B. Angina is acute chest pain when the blood circulation to the brain is reduced. C. Persons with blood group-AB can donate blood to any person with any blood group under ABO system. D. Calcium ions play a very important role in blood clotting. Which two of the above
84115.sol: Arteries are the blood vessels which carry blood away from the heart. In comparison to veins, arteries have narrow lumen and more muscular thick walls to bear the pressure of pumping action of heart. Angina is constricting chest pain caused due to reduced blood supply to the heart wall. Persons with blood group-AB are universal acceptor, while those with blood group-O are universal donor. Calcium ions are required during blood clotting for the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin, and fibrinogen into fibrin.

84130.subject: Zoology
84130.text: Which of the following substances, if introduced into the blood stream, would cause coagulation of blood at the site of its introduction?
84130.sol: Thrombin acts as an enzyme and catalyses fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) into an insoluble fibre like polymer, fibrin. These fibres form a dense network upon the wound and trap blood corpuscles (WBCs, RBCs and platelets) and thus form a clot. Proteolytic cleavage of prothrombin generates thrombin, which converts fibrinogen into fibrin for clot formation. Fibrinogen is a protein produced by the liver which helps stop bleeding by helping blood clots to form. Heparin is used to prevent blood clots from forming.

Infection of typhoid bacteria stimulates the production of immuno-specific agglutinins, which are released in blood plasma.

Globular proteins have multiple functions as they are used to form enzymes, cellular messengers, and amino aci
120907.sol: Correct Option is : (D) Globular proteins have multiple functions as they are used to form enzymes, cellular messengers, and amino acids , while Fibrous proteins act only as structural proteins.

121150.subject: Botany
121150.text: As we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics
121150.sol: Can you recall the basis of the arrangement? Say, for example, as we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing. Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level. Hence, the problem of classification becomes more complex.

121189.subject: Botany
121189.text: Taxonomy and Related Terms Definitions A. Classification 1. The process of classifying organisms B. Nomenclature 2. The process of naming organisms C. Taxonomy 3. The study of relationships among organisms D. Systematics 4. The method of grouping organisms into categories
121189.sol: Classification is the method of grouping organisms into categories. Nomenclature is the process of naming organisms. Taxonomy involves the process of classifying organisms. Systematics is the study of relationships among organisms.

121417.subject: Botany
121417.text: Which group of Protists does this organism belong to?

121568.subject: Botany
121568.text: Read the given descriptions of two organisms, X and Y: Organism X is marine and photosynthetic, appearing yellow, green, brown, blue, or red depending on the main pigments present in its cells. Organism Y is found in stagnant water, photosynthesises in the presence of sunlight, but predates on smaller organisms when deprived of sunlight. Select the correct statement regarding the cell wall or outer covering of organi
options: X has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface, while Y lacks a cell wall and has a protein-rich pellicle.
X has overlapping silica shells, while Y has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
X lacks a cell wall and has a protein-rich pellicle, while Y has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
Both X and Y possess a cellulosic cell wall, but only Y has a protein-rich pellicle.
121568.sol: Based on the given descriptions, organism X is a dinoflagellate because they are mostly marine, photosynthetic, and appear in various colours depending on their pigments. Organism Y is a euglenoid because they are found in stagnant water and exhibit mixotrophic nutrition (photosynthetic in light, heterotrophic in dark). Dinoflagellates (X) have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface of their cell wall. Euglenoids (Y) lack a cell wall; instead, they have a protein-rich layer called a pellicle which makes their

121762.subject: Botany
121762.text: Why are bryophytes called amphibians of the plant kingdom?
options: They can live in soil but need water for sexual reproduction.
They are found in both freshwater and marine environments.
They have a two-stage life cycle.
121762.sol: Bryophytes include the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. They usually occur in damp, humid and shaded localities. They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks/soil. The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attach

121846.subject: Botany
121846.text: How are the seeds of angiosperms enclosed?
121846.sol: Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes. The pollen grain is released from the microsporangium. They are carried in air currents and come in contact with the opening of the ovules borne on megasporophylls. The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards archegonia in the ovules and discharges their contents near the mouth of the archegonia. Following

121871.subject: Botany
121871.text: Identify and name the plant and its division, choose the correct option:

122576.subject: Botany
122576.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Features) List II (Taxa) A. Flame cells for osmoregulation I. Reptilia B. Muscular pharynx II. Chondrichthyes C. Placoid scales III. Aschelminthes D. Epidermal scales or scutes IV. Platyhelminthes Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
122576.sol: Platyhelminthes have specialised cells called flame cells which help in osmoregulation and excretion. Aschelminthes have a complete alimentary canal with a well-developed muscular pharynx. Members of class Chondrichthyes have tough skin containing minute placoid scales. Members of class Reptilia have their body covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes. Therefore, the correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I. Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

122685.subject: Botany
122685.sol: Trochophore is cilliated, larval stage of polychaetes, mollsucs and rotifers. Neopilina, Chiton and Pila belong to phylum-Molusca. Molluscan development is either direct or with metamorphosis through the trochophore stage.

123402.subject: Botany
123402.text: How is the study of plant anatomy useful to us?
options: to know which plant to consume
to know when the plant will die
to know about the internal structures which show adaptations to diverse environment
123402.sol: It is important to study plant anatomy to know about the internal structures which show adaptations to diverse environment.

123606.subject: Botany
123606.text: How are the chromosomes connected to spindle fibres during metaphase?
123606.sol: By this stage, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope. This then, is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied. At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that

123623.subject: Botany
123623.text: What happens to the nuclear envelope at the end of telophase?
options: It develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei
It reforms with the help of the nucleolus
It attaches to the centromeres of the chromosomes
123623.sol: The individual chromosomes can no longer be seen and each set of chromatin material tends to collect at each of the two poles. This is the stage which shows the following key events:  Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements.  Nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei.  Nucleolus, golgi complex and ER reform.

123850.subject: Botany
123850.text: In oocytes of some vertebrates, a specific stage of meiosis I can last for months or years. Identify this arrested stage and the specific structure that holds the homologous chromosomes together during this prolonged phase.
123850.sol: According to NCERT, in oocytes of some vertebrates, the diplotene stage can last for months or years. During the beginning of diplotene, the synaptonemal complex dissolves. The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossing over. These X-shaped structures where the chromosomes remain physically attached are called chiasmata. Therefore, during this prolonged arrested phase, it is the chiasmata that hold the homologous chromosomes together, not the

124292.subject: Botany
124292.text: Chromoplasts impart yellow, orange, or red colours to various parts of the plant such as flowers and fruits. Which of the following accurately describes the nature of the pigments stored in these plastids?
options: Fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene and xanthophylls
124292.sol: According to NCERT, chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls, and others. These pigments are responsible for imparting yellow, orange, or red colours to plant parts. Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments, but they are found in the vacuole, not in plastids. Chlorophylls are fat-soluble pigments primarily found in chloroplasts, responsible for trapping light energy. Answer: Fat-soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene and xanthophylls

124320.subject: Botany
124320.text: Read the following statement and choose the option that correctly fills the blanks (A) and (B). In some prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, there are membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called ___(A)___ which contain pigments, whereas in most bacteria, the membranous extensions that help in cell wall formation and DNA replication are called ___(B)___.
124320.sol: In prokaryotic cells, the plasma membrane extends into the cytoplasm to form specialized structures. In cyanobacteria, these membranous extensions are called chromatophores, which contain pigments involved in photosynthesis. Thus, (A) is Chromatophores. In most other bacteria, the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell form a special membranous structure called the mesosome. Mesosomes help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells. Thus, (B) is Mesosomes. Thylakoids are fo

124587.subject: Botany
124587.text: Which of the following processes is initiated by ethylene in peanut seeds?
124587.sol: Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, sprouting of potato tubers. Ethylene is used to initiate flowering and for synchronising fruit-set in pineapples. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of the fruits.

125265.subject: Botany
125265.text: Assertion : Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in legume root nodules survive in oxygen-depleted cells of nodules. Reason : Legheamoglobin completely removes oxygen from the nodule cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
125265.sol: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation occurs in legume plants. It takes place in the Rhizobium bacteroids which are located within root nodules cells. The important enzyme Nitrogenase (synthesised by Rhizobium ) that reduces N ₂ , is oxygen sensitive. It can only function at low oxygen concentration. This low oxygen concentration in bacteriod is provided by leghaemoglobin. Leghaemoglobin (pink in colour) is a form of pigment found in the nitrogen fixing root nodules of legume. It binds oxygen and thus protects the nitrogen f

125400.subject: Botany
125400.text: What does the accumulation of protons in the lumen contribute to in photosynthesis?
125400.sol: The NADP reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the membrane. Along with electrons that come from the acceptor of electrons of PS I, protons are necessary for the reduction of NADP+ to NADPH+ H+ . These protons are also removed from the stroma. Hence, within the chloroplast, protons in the stroma decrease in number, while in the lumen there is accumulation of protons. This creates a proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane as well as a measurable decrease in pH in the lumen. This gradient is importa

125806.subject: Botany
125806.text: What is the innermost wall layer of a microsporangium called?
125806.sol: The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains. Structure of microsporangium: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium appears near circular in outline. It is generally surrounded by four wall layers the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum. The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen. The innermost wall laye

126378.subject: Botany
126378.text: The cavity of diencephalon is known as
126378.sol: Diencephalon is situated between the cerebral hemispheres above and midbrain below. Its cavity known as the third ventricle or diocoel is connected to each lateral ventricle of cerebral hemisphere by foramen of Monro, separately.

126463.subject: Botany
126463.text: What is the purpose of extracting compounds from living tissues?
options: To isolate and purify a compound
To determine the molecular formula and structure
126463.sol: One extracts the compounds, then subjects the extract to various separation techniques till one has separated a compound from all other compounds. In other words, one isolates and purifies a compound. Analytical techniques, when applied to the compound give us an idea of the molecular formula and the probable structure of the compound. All the carbon compounds that we get from living tissues can be called ‘biomolecules’.

126475.subject: Botany
126475.text: What is the reducing end of a polysaccharide chain?
126475.sol: In a polysaccharide chain (say glycogen), the right end is called the reducing end and the left end is called the non-reducing end. It has branches too. Starch forms helical secondary structures. In fact, starch can hold I2 molecules in the helical portion. The starch-I2 is blue in colour. Cellulose does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold I2.

126878.subject: Botany
126878.text: Telomerase is an enzyme which is a:
126878.sol: Telomerase is an ribonucleoprotein enzyme that works as a cellular reverse transcriptase that adds DNA in the chromosomal. It involves the protection of chromosome endings from getting shorter during replication of DNA to avoid the loss of catastrophic DNA. Related Theory Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein molecule that is enzymatic in nature. It uses a special mechanism for the synthesis of DNA at telomeric ends. The DNA repeat sequence of telomere has one G -rich strand and other C rich strand. The G-rich strand h

126918.subject: Botany
126918.sol: Macromolecule chitin is an example complex structural hetero polysaccharide. It has nitrogen containing glucose derivatives such as N -acetyl glycosamine. It is present as the structural component of fungal cell walls and exoskeleton of arthropods etc.

127186.subject: Botany
127186.text: Which species are facing the threat of extinction globally?
127186.sol: Extinctions across taxa are not random; some groups like amphibians appear to be more vulnerable to extinction. Adding to the grim scenario of extinctions is the fact that more than 15,500 species world-wide are facing the threat of extinction. Presently, 12 per cent of all bird species, 23 per cent of all mammal species, 32 per cent of all amphibian species and 31 per cent of all gymnosperm species in the world face the threat of extinction

127334.subject: Botany
127334.text: Hypothesis Explanation A. Speciation Time 1. Tropical environments are more constant and predictable. B. Constant Environment 2. More solar energy available in the tropics contributes to higher productivity. C. Solar Energy 3. Tropics have had a long evolutionary time without frequent disturbances. D. Productivity 4. Species richness increases with increasing explored area.
127334.sol: A - 3: Speciation is generally a function of time, with tropics having had a long evolutionary time. B - 1: Tropical environments are less seasonal and more predictable. C - 2: More solar energy in the tropics contributes to higher productivity. D - 4: The species-area relationship shows increased species richness with increasing explored area.

127451.subject: Botany
127451.text: In the following, in each set, a conservation approach and an example of a method of conservation are given (a) In situ conservation-Biosphere Reserve (b) Ex situ conservation-Sacred groves (c) In situ conservation-Seed bank (d) Ex situ conservation-Cryopreservation Select the option with a correct match of approach and method:
127451.sol: In-situ conservation: The In–situ strategies emphasis protection of whole ecosystem. Examples are national parks, wild life sancturies, biosphere reserves and sacred grooves. Ex-situ conservation: In this type of conservation strategies, threatened animals and plants are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care. Examples are seed bank, cryopreservation, botanical gardens, and zoological parks.

127578.subject: Botany
options: The process of breaking down organic matter into inorganic substances
The process of breaking down organic matter into water
The process of breaking down organic matter into nitrogen
The process of breaking down organic matter into humus
127578.sol: Decomposition refers to the process of breaking down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients. You may have heard of the earthworm being referred to as the farmer’s ‘friend’. This is so because they help in the breakdown of complex organic matter as well as in loosening of the soil. Similarly , decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients and the process is called decomposition. Dead plant remains su

127590.subject: Botany
127590.text: Do ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to maintain order?
127590.sol: Ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness as stated by the Second Law of Thermodynamics. Further, ecosystems are not exempt from the Second Law of thermodynamics. They need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require, to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness .The green plant in the ecosystem are called producers. In a terrestrial ecosystem, major producers are herbaceous and woody plants. Li

127736.subject: Botany
127736.text: Concept Explanation A. Unidirectional flow of energy 1. Energy flows from sun to producers to consumers B. First Law of Thermodynamics 2. Energy is conserved in a system C. Second Law of Thermodynamics 3. Systems tend to increase in entropy D. Detritus Food Chain 4. Begins with dead organic matter
127736.sol: Unidirectional flow of energy (A) refers to the energy flow from the sun to producers to consumers (1). The First Law of Thermodynamics (B) states that energy is conserved in a system (2). The Second Law of Thermodynamics (C) indicates that systems tend to increase in entropy (3). The Detritus Food Chain (D) begins with dead organic matter (4).

127808.subject: Botany
127808.text: A researcher is constructing an ecological pyramid for a forest ecosystem but encounters a difficulty: a particular species of bird in the forest feeds on both plant seeds and herbivorous insects. Which specific limitation of ecological pyramids is best highlighted by this difficulty?
options: Ecological pyramids do not accommodate a food web
It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels
It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature
Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids
127808.sol: By feeding on plant seeds, the bird acts as a primary consumer (second trophic level). By feeding on herbivorous insects, the bird acts as a secondary consumer (third trophic level). Ecological pyramids are constructed with each organism assigned to a single trophic level. The difficulty in placing this bird in the pyramid directly highlights the limitation that ecological pyramids do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels. Answer: It does not take into account the same speci

128807.subject: Zoology
128807.text: What are the two natural antibodies that are present in the plasma of different individuals?
128807.sol: : ABO grouping is based on the presence or absence of two surface antigens (chemicals that can induce immune response) on the RBCs namely A and B. Similarly, the plasma of different individuals contain two natural antibodies (proteins produced in response to antigens). The distribution of antigens and antibodies in the four groups of blood, A, B, AB and O are given in Table 15.1. You probably know that during blood transfusion, any blood cannot be used; the blood of a donor has to be carefully matched with the bloo

128829.subject: Zoology
128829.text: What initiates the mechanism of coagulation?
128829.sol: Blood exhibits coagulation or clotting in response to an injury or trauma. This is a mechanism to prevent excessive loss of blood from the body. You would have observed a dark reddish brown scum formed at the site of a cut or an injury over a period of time. It is a clot or coagulam formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thrombins, in turn a

129162.subject: Zoology
129162.text: Which of the following substances, if introduce in the blood stream, would cause coagulation, at the site of its introduction?
129162.sol: Lipoproteinaceous, thromboplastin is released by the injured tissue. This reacts with Ca ²⁺ ions present in blood and forms a proteinaceous enzyme called prothrombinase. Later in the presence of Ca ²⁺ inactivates heparin (anticoagulant) and catalyses prothrombin (inactive plasma protein) into an active thrombin protein. Thrombin acts as an enzyme and catalyses fibrinogen (a soluble plasma protein) into an insoluble fibre like polymer, fibrin. These fibres form a dense network upon the wound and trap blood corpuscle

129404.subject: Zoology
129404.text: Examine the diagram of the two cell types A and B given below and select the correct option
options: Cell A is the rod cell found evenly all over retina
Cell A is the cone cell more concentrated in the fovea centralis
Cell B is concerned with colour vision in bright light
Cell A is sensitive to low light intensities
129404.sol: Cone cell is one of two types (other is rod) of light sensitive cells in the retina of the eye. The human retina contains 6-7 million cones which function best in bright light and are essential for active vision (receiving a sharp accurate image). The area of retina called the fovea contains the greatest concentration of cone. Cones can also distinguish colours. There are 3 types of cone, each sensitive to the wavelength of a different primary colour - red, green or blue.

129490.subject: Zoology
129490.text: What is the glomerulus along with Bowman's capsule called?
129490.sol: The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus. Glomerulus alongwith Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle (Figure 16.4). The tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network – proximal convoluted tubule (PCT). A hairpin shaped Henle’s loop is the next part of the tubule which has a descending and an ascending limb. The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted

129944.subject: Zoology
129944.text: Identify A and B from the following figure
options: A and B both are pulmonary veins.
A and B both are pulmonary arteries.
A is Pulmonary Vein and B is Pulmonary Artery.
B is Pulmonary Vein and A is Pulmonary Artery.
129944.sol: B is Pulmonary Vein, containing Oxygenated blood and A is Pulmonary Artery containing deoxygenated blood.

129956.subject: Zoology
129956.text: In the following figure, what does Y and X represent?
options: X is % saturation of haemoglobin with carbon monoxide and Y is Partial pressure of Oxygen
X is % saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen and Y is Partial pressure of carbon dioxide
X is % saturation of haemoglobin with carbon monoxide and Y is Partial pressure of carbon dioxide
X is % saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen and Y is Partial pressure of Oxygen
129956.sol: [D]X is % saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen and Y is Partial pressure of Oxygen.

130641.subject: Zoology
130641.text: Apart from preventing pregnancy, male condoms also protect against:
130641.sol: Such methods are available for both males and females. Condoms (Figure 3.1 a, b) are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.

130683.subject: Zoology
130683.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Genital herpes is completely curable Reason: Using condoms can lead to STIs
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
130683.sol: Genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Early symptoms of most of these are minor and include itching,fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc., in the genital region. Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence, may remain undetected for long.

130694.subject: Zoology
130694.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Progestogens can be used by males as injections to avoid pregnancy 2. Surgical interventions allow gametes to pass efficiently 3. Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives 4. Saheli –the new oral contraceptive for the females con
130694.sol: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives as they could be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

130951.subject: Zoology
130951.text: What are the components of a normal human sperm?
options: Head, neck, a middle piece and tail
Mons pubis, labia majora and labia minora
130951.sol: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail (Figure 2.6). A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of sperm. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome.

131246.subject: Zoology
131246.text: A pregnant woman undergoes a routine ultrasound examination at exactly 12 weeks of gestation. Which of the following accurately describes the developmental status of the foetus at this specific stage?
options: Most of the major organ systems are formed, including well-developed limbs and external genital organs.
The foetus develops limbs and digits, but the major organ systems are not yet well-developed.
The first movements of the foetus are observed along with the appearance of hair on the head.
The body is covered with fine hair, the eyelids separate, and eyelashes are formed.
131246.sol: According to NCERT, the gestation period in humans is characterised by specific developmental milestones. At exactly 12 weeks (the end of the first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed. For example, the limbs and external genital organs are well-developed. The development of limbs and digits occurs earlier, by the end of the second month ( 8 weeks). The first movements of the foetus and the appearance of hair on the head are observed during the fifth month (approx. 20 weeks). The body is covered w

131295.subject: Zoology
131295.text: The entry of a sperm into a secondary oocyte induces the completion of its meiotic division. Which of the following represents the immediate cellular products of this specific division?
options: A secondary oocyte and a first polar body
An ootid and a second polar body
A primary oocyte and a second polar body
131295.sol: The entry of a sperm into the secondary oocyte breaks its arrest at metaphase II and induces the completion of the second meiotic division. This second meiotic division is unequal and results in the formation of a large haploid cell called the ootid (or ovum) and a tiny second polar body. The formation of a secondary oocyte and a first polar body occurs upon the completion of the first meiotic division prior to ovulation. Oogenesis in humans is characterized by unequal divisions, hence two equal-sized ova are never

131537.subject: Zoology
131537.text: Who helped decipher the code with the help of a cell-free system for protein synthesis?
131537.sol: Providing proof that the codon was a triplet, was a more daunting task. The chemical method developed by Har Gobind Khorana was instrumental in synthesizing RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases (homopolymers and copolymers). Marshall Nirenberg’s cell-free system for protein synthesis finally helped the code to be deciphered. Severo Ochoa enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) was also helpful in polymerising RNA with defined sequences in a template independent manner (enzymatic synthesis of RNA).

131779.subject: Zoology
131779.text: In E.coli, the lac operon gets switched on when:
options: lactose is present and it binds to the repressor
RNA polymerase binds to the operator
lactose is present and it binds to RNA polymerase
131779.sol: Presence of lactose switches on lac operon as allolactose removes the repressor for RNA polymerase to bind.

131785.subject: Zoology
131785.text: Who revealed the biochemical nature of the transforming principle?
131785.sol: Avery, Mcleod and McCarty noticed that the RNA digesting enzyme (RNases), Protein digesting enzymes (Proteases) did not affect the transformation of the non-virulent R-strain to the virulent S-strain.

131867.subject: Zoology
131867.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the enzymes involved in eukaryotic transcription and their products. List-I List-II A. RNA polymerase I I. hnRNA B. RNA polymerase II II. 28S rRNA C. RNA polymerase III III. tRNA and snRNAs Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
131867.sol: In eukaryotes, there are three major types of RNA polymerases in the nucleus, each with specific functions. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S). Therefore, A matches with II. RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, known as heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). Therefore, B matches with I. RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs (small nuclear RNAs). Therefore, C matches with III. The correct matching sequence is A-II, B-I, C-III. Answer: A-

132469.subject: Zoology
132469.text: Read the following statements carefully regarding sickle-cell anaemia: (I) It is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are carrier for the gene. (II) The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid by Valine at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. (III) The mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes poly
132469.sol: Statement (I) is correct: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome linked recessive trait. Statement (II) is correct: The molecular basis of the disease is a point mutation leading to the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain. Statement (III) is incorrect: The mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes polymerisation under LOW oxygen tension, not high oxygen tension. This polymerisation changes the RBC shape from a biconcave disc to an elongated sickle-like structur

132909.subject: Zoology
132909.text: Which of the following evolutionary concepts is incorrectly matched with its example?
options: Vestigial organ - Nictitating membrane in humans
132909.sol: Wisdom teeth (third molars) in humans are vestigial organs, not an example of atavism. Vestigial organs are those which are present in a reduced form and are useless to the possessor, but were fully developed and functional in the ancestors. Atavism refers to the sudden reappearance of an ancestral trait that had been lost during evolution (e.g., a short tail in a newborn baby or dense body hair). Limulus (King crab) is a classic example of a living fossil. Archaeopteryx is a connecting link between reptiles and bi

132931.subject: Zoology
132931.text: Read the following characteristics regarding a human ancestor: (i) It was the first human-like being the hominid. (ii) Its brain capacity was between 650-800 cc . (iii) It probably did not eat meat. Identify the hominid from the given options:
132931.sol: According to NCERT, Homo habilis was the first human-like being the hominid. Its brain capacity was between 650-800 cc and they probably did not eat meat. Australopithecus had a smaller brain capacity and essentially ate fruit. Homo erectus had a brain capacity of 900 cc and probably ate meat. Neanderthal man had a brain size of 1400 cc and used hides to protect their body. Answer: Homo habilis

To increase the number of HIV-infected people
To reduce the spread of HIV
133273.sol: AIDS is caused by the Human ImmunoDeficiency Virus (HIV).People who are at high risk of getting HIV infection include individuals with multiple sexual partners, drug addicts who take drugs intravenously, individuals who require repeated blood transfusions, and children born to an HIV-infected mother.The spread of HIV infection is due to conscious behavior patterns and not due to natural causes or poor monitoring. Regular check-ups for HIV in susceptible populations aim to reduce the spread of the disease. Society p

133341.subject: Zoology
133341.text: The main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced is
133341.sol: The bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced. The thymus is a lobed organ located near the heart and beneath the breastbone. The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age and by the time puberty is attained it reduces to a very small size. Both bone-marrow and thymus provide micro-environments for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes

133433.subject: Zoology
133433.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. HIV/AIDS is not spread by touch or physical contact; it only spreads through body fluids. 2. HIV/AIDS-infected individuals should not be isolated from their family and society for their physical and psychological well-being. 3. There is typically a time-lag between HIV infection and the appearance of AIDS symptoms, which can range from a few months to ma
133433.sol: It is important to note that HIV/AIDS is not spread by mere touch or physical contact; it spreads only through body fluids. It is, hence, imperative, for the physical and psychological well-being, that the HIV/AIDS infected persons are not isolated from family and society. There is always a time-lag between the infection and appearance of AIDS symptoms. This period may vary from a few months to many years (usually 5-10 years).

133490.subject: Zoology
133490.text: The term ‘Health’ is defined in many ways. The most accurate definition of health would be:
options: Health is the state of body and mind in a balanced condition
Health is the reflection of a smiling face
Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being
Health is a symbol of economic prosperity.
133490.sol: The most accurate definition of health is that it is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being.

133574.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Malignant tumors exhibit metastasis, which is considered the most feared property of cancer. Reason (R): Neoplastic cells in malignant tumors grow very rapidly, invading and damaging surrounding normal tissues by starving them of vital nutrients. In the light of the above statements, choose the mos
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
133574.sol: Assertion (A) is true because malignant tumors have cells that slough off and reach distant sites through blood, forming new tumors wherever they lodge. This property, called metastasis, is the most feared property of cancer. Reason (R) is also true because cells of malignant tumors grow rapidly, invading and damaging surrounding normal tissues. As these cells actively divide and grow, they also starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients. However, Reason (R) explains the local damage and competitive g

133577.subject: Zoology
133577.text: A patient was diagnosed with a primary tumor in the liver. A few months later, secondary tumors were discovered in the lungs. Based on this clinical presentation, identify the nature of the primary tumor and the specific term used to describe this phenomenon of spreading.
133577.sol: The spread of a tumor from its primary site (liver) to distant organs (lungs) indicates that the tumor is not confined to its original location. Therefore, it is a malignant tumor. The property of malignant cells sloughing off and reaching distant sites through the blood to form secondary tumors is called metastasis. Benign tumors remain confined to their original location and do not metastasize. Contact inhibition is a property of normal cells, which is lost in cancer cells. Answer: Malignant tumor, Metastasis

134289.sol: The gene cryIIAb encodes a Bt toxin protein that specifically targets and controls the cotton bollworm. When the insect ingests the plant tissue, the Bt toxin exists as an inactive protoxin. It is converted into an active form of toxin due to the alkaline pH of the insect's midgut, which solubilises the protein crystals. 134840.subject: Zoology
134840.text: A researcher programs a thermal cycler for a PCR reaction with the following temperature profile for 30 cycles: 94^ C for 1 minute 85^ C for 1 minute 72^ C for 2 minutes The PCR fails to amplify the gene of interest. What is the most likely reason for this failure?
options: The double-stranded DNA will fail to separate into single strands at 94^ C .
The primers will fail to form stable hydrogen bonds with the template DNA at 85^ C .
The Taq polymerase enzyme will denature and permanently lose its catalytic activity at 85^ C .
The extension step will occur normally, but with a very high rate of mutation.
134840.sol: The three steps of a PCR cycle are Denaturation, Annealing, and Extension. Step 1 ( 94^ C ) is the denaturation step, which successfully separates the double-stranded DNA. Step 2 ( 85^ C ) is intended to be the annealing step. However, the optimum temperature for primer annealing is typically between 40^ C and 60^ C . At a high temperature of 85^ C , the short oligonucleotide primers possess too much kinetic energy to form stable hydrogen bonds with the complementary regions of the template DNA. Without annealed pr

135021.subject: Zoology
135021.sol: Gene transfer is present in biolistics. This technique involves firing of microscopic gold particles coated with the foreign DNA at the cells using a compressed air gun. It is designed to overcome the problem of strong cell wall in plant tissues. These particles can penetrate the cell wall, the cell and the nuclear membrane to deliver the DNA to the nucleus.

An individual is either a male or a female but a population has a sex ratio (e.g., 60 percent of the population are females and 40 per cent males). A population at any given time is composed of individuals of different ages. If the age distribution (percent individuals of a given age or age group) is plotted for the population, the resulting structure is called an age pyramid (Figure 11.1). Orchid and Mango tree III. Commensalism (epiphyte) D. Cattle Egret and Grazing Cattle IV. Mutualism (oviposition in inflorescence) Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
135350.sol: Fig and Wasp exhibit mutualism where the wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while using it for oviposition (egg-laying). 135371.subject: Zoology
135371.text: Read the following description of a plant-pollinator interaction: "In a Mediterranean plant, one floral part bears an uncanny resemblance to a female insect in size, colour, and markings. The male insect is attracted to what it perceives as a female, and during pseudocopulation, gets dusted with pollen from the flower." Identify the plant and the specific ecological phenomenon it exhibits.
135371.sol: The given description refers to the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys , which employs a mechanism known as 'sexual deceit' to achieve pollination. In this phenomenon, one petal of the flower mimics the female bee. The male bee is deceived and attempts to copulate with the flower (pseudocopulation), inadvertently transferring pollen in the process. options: exactly towards the centre of the circular path
exactly along the tangent to the circular path
at an acute angle to the direction of its instantaneous velocity
at an obtuse angle to the direction of its instantaneous velocity
6a13e465688ac6d0667aacfb.sol: The particle is moving in a circular path, so it experiences a centripetal force F _c directed towards the centre of the circle, which is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity v . Since the speed of the particle is continuously increasing, there is a tangential force F _t acting in the direction of the instantaneous velocity v . Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f6c.sol: Statement I is correct because 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols react immediately with Lucas reagent (a mixture of concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂ ) at room temperature to form insoluble alkyl chlorides, which appear as turbidity. Statement II is incorrect because the reaction of tertiary alcohols with Lucas reagent proceeds via an S_N1 mechanism, which involves the formation of a stable tertiary carbocation. Therefore, tertiary alcohols are the most reactive, not sterically unhinde

6a252ff398efbb6c17e929ef.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : In recombinant DNA technology, it is essential to cut both the vector DNA and the source DNA with the same restriction endonuclease. Reason (R) : Cutting both DNA molecules with the same restriction enzyme produces complementary sticky ends that facilitate their joining by DNA ligase. In the ligh
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
6a252ff398efbb6c17e929ef.sol: In recombinant DNA technology, the vector DNA and the source DNA must be cut with the same restriction endonuclease. This ensures that both DNA molecules have complementary sticky ends. The complementary sticky ends can then base-pair with each other and are subsequently joined by the enzyme DNA ligase to form a recombinant DNA molecule. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

95251.subject: Botany
95251.text: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axis and appear later than primary meristem, is called
95251.sol: The meristem that occurs in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axis and appear later than primary meristem, is called secondary or lateral meristem. They are cylindrical meristems and are responsible for producing the secondary tissue.

95469.subject: Botany
95469.text: Which one of the following statement is totally wrong about the occurrence of notochord, while the other three are correct?
options: It is present only in larval tail in Ascidians
It is replaced by a vertebral column in adult frog
It is absent throughout life in humans from the very beginning
It is present throughout life in Amphioxus
95469.sol: The notochord is a flexible rod-like structure that forms the main support of the body in the lowest chordates. It is not absent in humans throughout their life. The notochord is present in the embryonic stage and gets changed or replaced by the vertebral column in the adult.

95541.subject: Botany
95541.text: Four characters (a-d) are given below. Which two are CORRECT about phylum arthropoda? (i) It is the largest phylum of animal kingdom. (ii) One third of all named species on earth are arthropods. (iii) They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and segmented animals. (iv) The body is covered by calcareous exoskeleton.
95541.sol: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of animal kingdom. These include two third of all the animals on the earth. Majority of animals in this phylum are insects. 'Arthros' means joins and 'poda' means feet and hence these animals have jointed appendages. The body is divided into head, thorax and abdomen. These animals have proper organ systems, triploblastic body and are Eucoelomates. Their body is covered by exoskeleton made up of chitin.

95642.subject: Botany
95642.text: Lichens are ecologically important as they
options: Are symbionts of algae and fungi
95642.sol: Lichens play the role of pioneer species in primary succession on rocks. Lichens secrete acids to dissolve rocks and thus help in weathering and soil formation. Later on lichens make favourable conditions for the growth of very small plants like bryophytes, which are able to hold small amount of soil. Lichens are also SO 2 pollution indicators.

was discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971
95848.sol: Viroids are the smallest infectious pathogens known, consisting solely of short strands of circular, single-stranded RNA without protein coats. They are mostly plant pathogens, some of which are of economical importance. Viroid genomes are extremely small in size, ranging from 246 to 467 nucleobases. 6a7a1ff8fe2f6ce3ab4ed4d6.text: Arrange the following alkaline earth metals in the increasing order of their density: Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba
6a7a1ff8fe2f6ce3ab4ed4d6.sol: The density of alkaline earth metals does not show a regular trend down the group. From Be to Ca , the density decreases because the increase in atomic volume is more prominent than the increase in atomic mass. However, from Ca to Ba , the density increases as the increase in atomic mass outweighs the increase in atomic volume. The actual densities (in g/cm ^3 ) are approximately: Be ( 1.84 ), Mg ( 1.74 ), Ca ( 1.55 ), Sr ( 2.63 ), and Ba ( 3.59 ). Therefore, the correct increasing order of density is Ca Answer: Ca
